attackPath.dataflow: Anonymous JSON body -> POST /api/contact -> verifyTurnstile missing-secret branch -> verification guard passes -> authenticated Resend request
attackPath.reachability: A remote unauthenticated caller can trigger the path when mail delivery is configured and exactly one Turnstile half is configured. The destination remains fixed to the site owner.

codeEvidence.explanation: The helper treats every missing secret as disabled mode, even when the public site key says verification is expected.
codeEvidence.label: Absent secret is accepted

codeEvidence.explanation: A true result carries the anonymous submission through the apparent verification guard to authenticated email delivery.
codeEvidence.label: Verification result gates Resend

confidence.rationale: Direct source review and a local mocked-delivery harness confirmed that the partial configuration accepts a missing token and reaches the delivery boundary.

preventiveControls: Validate paired security configuration in CI and deployment documentation.
Use explicit verification timeouts and fail closed for configured Turnstile.
findings.remediation: Require the public site key and private secret to be present or absent together, return a generic 503 for partial configuration, and fail closed on verification errors and timeouts.
remediationTests: Public site key only returns 503 and never calls Siteverify or Resend.
Private secret only returns 503 and never calls Siteverify or Resend.
Both keys present require a valid mocked token; both absent follow the documented disabled policy.

rootCause.summary: The client and server infer one security mode from two independent environment variables, and the server maps an absent secret directly to success instead of rejecting an inconsistent configuration.

severity.changeConditions: Severity would rise if the endpoint gained an attacker-selected recipient or privileged action, and would fall to informational if deployment validation proved partial Turnstile configuration impossible.
severity.rationale: An unauthenticated Internet caller can bypass the advertised bot check only in a partial deployment configuration. The result is fixed-recipient spam and provider-quota use; no data disclosure, privilege gain, or arbitrary recipient is available.

findings.summary: When the public Turnstile site key is present but the server secret is absent, the contact UI advertises a bot challenge while the API treats tokenless submissions as verified and can reach email delivery.
findings.title: Partial Turnstile configuration fails open in the contact API

checklist: Confirmed the public anonymous entry point.
Exercised public-key-only, both-key, and both-absent configurations.
Confirmed no live provider or deployment was contacted.
validation.method: Static source trace plus a local dependency-free control-flow probe with a mocked delivery sink.
validation.remainingUncertainty: The reviewed production environment had Turnstile disabled; future dashboard changes can create the vulnerable partial state.

attackPath.dataflow: Anonymous request -> instance-local Map lookup -> fresh per-instance allowance -> schema and optional verification -> authenticated Resend request
attackPath.reachability: A remote caller benefits from concurrency, scaling, regional routing, or routine instance replacement. The attacker does not need to spoof Vercel-normalized forwarding headers.

codeEvidence.explanation: Every JavaScript instance owns a separate Map, so the security budget is neither global nor durable.
codeEvidence.label: Quota state is process-local

codeEvidence.explanation: A fresh instance's allow decision permits another authenticated provider call for the same IP.
codeEvidence.label: Local decision gates email delivery

confidence.rationale: The state lifetime follows directly from the module-scoped Map, and a deterministic local model reproduced independent budgets and cold-start reset behavior.

preventiveControls: Document the platform-edge rate-limit rule as required production infrastructure.
Alert on contact 429 rates and email-provider quota anomalies.
findings.remediation: Enforce the authoritative POST /api/contact budget in Vercel Firewall or an atomic durable rate-limit service; retain the bounded in-memory limiter only as a secondary burst guard.
remediationTests: Split six same-IP requests across two fresh limiter instances and require request six to fail.
Restart application state between request five and six and require request six to fail at the authoritative edge/store.
Verify atomic behavior under concurrent fifth-boundary submissions.

rootCause.summary: A global security invariant is assigned to ephemeral per-process memory in a horizontally scaled serverless runtime.

severity.changeConditions: Severity would rise if the downstream operation became higher-value or attacker-directed, and would fall if a verified platform-edge rule enforced one atomic global budget.
severity.rationale: An unauthenticated caller can exceed the intended email-abuse budget as serverless instances scale or recycle, but the effect is bounded to fixed-recipient nuisance mail and provider quota.

findings.summary: The five-per-hour contact budget is stored in a module-level Map, so each scaled or replacement serverless instance creates an independent budget for the same client IP.
findings.title: Instance-local contact rate limit can be bypassed across function instances

checklist: Confirmed one instance blocks request six.
Confirmed three independent instances allow fifteen requests and replacement state allows request six.
validation.method: Static source and deployment-lifecycle analysis plus a deterministic local multi-Map model.
validation.remainingUncertainty: No live production scaling or paid-provider traffic was exercised; exact instance routing frequency is platform-dependent.

attackPath.dataflow: Hostile web page -> cross-origin text/plain POST -> request.json -> schema and optional Turnstile -> authenticated Resend request
attackPath.reachability: A remote website can trigger the side effect from visitor browsers without a preflight when Turnstile is disabled or otherwise bypassed. Response contents remain unreadable to the hostile origin.

codeEvidence.explanation: request.json parses valid JSON bytes even when a hostile browser declares the safelisted text/plain media type and supplies a foreign Origin.
codeEvidence.label: Request is parsed without origin or media-type checks

codeEvidence.explanation: The server turns the accepted cross-origin body into an authenticated provider request; browser response-read restrictions occur too late to prevent the side effect.
codeEvidence.label: Parsed data reaches Resend

confidence.rationale: A hostile-Origin text/plain request against the local vulnerable server reached the delivery-configuration branch, proving that parsing, validation, and optional verification completed.

preventiveControls: Apply a restrictive CSP and frame-ancestors policy to the site.
Review every future state-changing route for explicit request-authority checks.
findings.remediation: Before rate limiting or parsing, require application/json, reject a foreign Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site, and return generic no-store errors without invoking Turnstile or Resend.
remediationTests: Accept same-origin application/json and ensure rejection paths never call Siteverify or Resend.

rootCause.summary: The route treats syntactically valid JSON as sufficient request authority and relies implicitly on browser CORS response policy instead of enforcing media type and trusted origin before parsing.

severity.changeConditions: Severity would rise if the route acquired a privileged user session or attacker-selected recipient, and would fall if strict media-type and trusted-origin gates ran before parsing.
severity.rationale: Any website can recruit visitor browsers to trigger the fixed-recipient contact action when Turnstile is disabled or bypassed, but the attacker cannot read the response, choose the recipient, or gain privilege.

findings.summary: The contact handler parses JSON without validating Origin or requiring application/json, allowing a hostile website to send a CORS-safelisted text/plain request that can reach email delivery without a preflight.
findings.title: Cross-origin text/plain requests can submit the contact form

checklist: Confirmed the route has no origin or media-type gate.
Reached the 503 delivery-configuration branch with external delivery deliberately disabled.
Verified the probe refuses non-loopback targets.
validation.method: Static source trace plus a local interface probe using a hostile Origin and CORS-safelisted text/plain JSON.
validation.remainingUncertainty: The exact behavior of every browser was not tested; the server-side acceptance was reproduced and follows the Fetch simple-request model.
